item.text: {"summary":"The forecast is internally coherent and has a clear persistence prior and ladder-derived 80% interval, but its resolver source field must match the canonical ledger binding.","requiredFixes":[{"rubricItem":"resolver","severity":"blocking","summary":"`resolutionSource` names BEA tables, while the canonical ledger target specifies the ALFRED DSPI CSV source binding as the resolver.","actionRequested":"Set `resolutionSource` to the canonical ledger wording: \"ALFRED DSPI CSV source binding for BEA disposable personal income first print\"; retain the BEA tables as underlying-producer context in reasoning."},{"rubricItem":"update","severity":"warning","summary":"The roughly +$118 billion June update is attributed to compensation and discounted farm income, but the cited evidence is primarily May and earlier releases rather than June-specific evidence.","actionRequested":"Either cite a dated, public June indicator or explicitly characterize the +$118 billion adjustment as a conservative extrapolation from the stated March–May reference class."},{"rubricItem":"interval","severity":"warning","summary":"The interval is ladder-derived and uncertainty sources are named, but the ladder width is not quantitatively tied to realized monthly DSPI volatility in the stated sample.","actionRequested":"State the realized March–May monthly-change dispersion/range and explain how it informed the 10th–90th ladder width, or explicitly justify the width as a scenario-based uncertainty allowance."}],"optionalSuggestions":["Use the canonical resolver wording verbatim wherever target metadata is validated.","Clarify that the March–May reference class is being used as monthly changes for volatility, rather than as level observations."]}
